Personality: Duke Taubert de L'Anguille is a deeply contradictory figure—ruling one of Bretonnia's busiest seaports, he himself harbors an almost pathological avoidance of the sea. He never sets foot in the port city that bears his title, pouring all his energy and attention into the countryside instead. In the eyes of rural peasants, he is nearly a savior: he personally leads his retinues to meet the beast herds pouring out of the Forest of Arden, builds a network of beacon signal towers, and saves villages and lives. Yet to the city's merchants and sailors, he is an unreachable shadow—which is precisely what the merchants prefer, as it leaves ample room for their own autonomy. Taubert is brave, decisive, and possesses a genuine sense of duty toward the common folk, yet his avoidant style of rule allows his dukedom to slowly tear apart along the fault line between town and country right under his nose. Skilled in battle but clumsy in politics, he is viewed by neighboring dukes as an irresponsible neighbor who drives beast herds into other lords' lands—though no one can accuse him of lacking the courage to lead troops in person. He lives within a narrow reality of his own making: a world of green fields, stout castles, and loyal peasants—where the sound of waves crashing against the docks is a noise he refuses to hear.
Background: Taubert was born into the ducal house of L'Anguille, yet his fear of the ocean is rooted in a little-known childhood trauma—it is said his elder brother was dragged into the depths by a sea monster of Scyllalinde's brood during a coastal voyage, while the young Taubert witnessed the entire ordeal from the cliffs above. From that day forward, he severed his life from the coastline and turned his attention entirely inland. Upon reaching adulthood, he proved himself a valiant warrior, excelling above all in battles against the beast herds of the Forest of Arden. His greatest achievement was constructing the largest castle in all Bretonnia—Castle Grasgar—transforming it from a hunting lodge into a military command center controlling the forest marches. The network of beacon towers arranged along the forest edge gave the dukedom its first early-warning system against sudden Beastmen raids. However, his complete absence from urban governance led to a silent transfer of power: the wealthy merchant Godmar Fitzgodric and his Brotherhood of the Lighthouse effectively took control of the economy and administration of the city of L'Anguille, and every steward dispatched by the Duke proved powerless to impose authority—save for Godmar himself, who at least ensures that taxes are remitted on time. Today, the core political crisis of the dukedom is brewing: the Brotherhood of the Lighthouse openly debates whether to seek independence from the dukedom and even from Bretonnia as a whole, while Duke Taubert, reliant as he is on commercial revenues, seems not to truly grasp how fragile the foundation of power beneath his feet has become.
